**Subject: Order TH-48217 — marked delivered but never received: resend or refund needed by Fri 13 Nov**

Dear Tiny Hands Edu Supplies Team,

I'm writing about order **TH-48217**, placed on **21 October**. I paid **R1,640** (including **R95 delivery**) by card for craft supplies for my class at **Bergview Pre-Primary in Plumstead**. The delivery address on the order was correct.

The courier's tracking shows my order as delivered on **Tuesday 3 November at 11:42, signed for by "M. Adams."** Nothing arrived. I checked with our gate guard, Uncle Faizel, who signs for and logs every school delivery in a book — there is no entry for the 3rd, no "M. Adams," and no package anywhere at the school. Nobody at Bergview has ever heard the name Adams.

Here's what I've already tried:

- **Emailed on 4 November and again on 6 November.** Both times I received the same copy-and-paste reply telling me the query "has been escalated to our courier partner."
- **Phoned on Friday.** After 38 minutes on hold, the advisor told me she couldn't do anything until the courier finishes its investigation, which could take 10 working days.

I don't think I should be left chasing this, and I don't think it's reasonable for me to keep waiting while I receive the same template. My contract is with Tiny Hands, not with the courier, and I never chose who delivered my order — so I'd like you to own this rather than pass me along again.

**What I need, in writing, is one of the following:**

1. A **replacement dispatch of the full order**, with a new tracking number and a confirmed delivery date; or
2. A **full refund of R1,640, including the R95 delivery fee**, back to my card.

Either way, I need an answer by **Friday 13 November**. Our end-of-year concert is on **27 November** and these supplies (6 tubs of finger paint, 4 bags of playdough, 200 paper plates, googly eyes, glitter glue, 2 rolls of brown paper) are for the props. The children have already made their masks, and I've been telling them the paint is "coming soon" for a week now — so this isn't theoretical, it has real consequences in my classroom and I have to plan around it.

A couple of other things I'd like on record. This was my **fourth order** from you and the first three went smoothly, which is exactly why I'm frustrated — not at the courier, but at the fact that R1,640 of my own money, spent on my teacher's salary for supplies for other people's children, has gone missing and I've been given a template twice and hold music once. I'd also like a **copy of the proof of delivery for the 3 November drop**, since the signature name doesn't match anyone at our school or in our records.

Please also let me know **who is handling this on your side**, and reply with a real person rather than an auto-response. A short, honest note about what happened and what you're doing is all I need.

If I don't hear back by Friday 13 November, I **will** dispute the payment with my bank and leave a review explaining what happened. I'd genuinely rather not — I'd rather keep ordering from you, and I have recommended you to other parents — but I do need this resolved.

Please confirm receipt of this email and tell me which of the two options you can commit to, and by when.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
Kindergarten Teacher
Bergview Pre-Primary, Plumstead, Cape Town
[Contact number]
**Order reference: TH-48217**
